observations: Source footprint: the five-page scaffold provides decision framing, a source-and-authority matrix, three issue analyses, alternatives and sensitivity, safeguards, open items, approval locator, and appendix index appropriate to a controller working memorandum.

Render and readability: fresh LibreOffice conversion preserved the native hash and produced five portrait pages; visual inspection of every release-owned page found stable tables, headings, wrapping, headers, and footers with no clipping or overlap.

Slot usability and consumer fit: declared tokens cover the full evidence-to-conclusion path and make missing content conspicuous, while the descriptor requires consumers to reject any instantiated document that retains a declared or double-brace token.

Authority separation: the body calls itself supporting analysis, the status and every footer state DRAFT - NOT APPROVED, open questions remain distinct from conclusions, and the approval field can record only an existing locator or that approval is not yet obtained.

Human-realism fit: the clean reviewed-working-copy layout is restrained rather than theatrically distressed; authorized instances can add role-appropriate review residue, but populated pagination and citation evidence must be generated anew.
Confidence limit: usability was assessed on the fact-free scaffold and its exact render; substantive citation accuracy and page flow remain instance-specific gates after authorized slot population.
summary: USABILITY_PASS: TMPL-0002 is a legible, appropriately structured internal decision-memo scaffold whose slot coverage and repeated non-approval signals make it suitable for controlled ANNA, Holodeck, and realism workflows. Each populated instance still needs fresh citation, leakage, authority, and pagination review.
